statement: The number 333...33 is written with twenty 3s, and it is multiplied by itself. What is the sum of the digits of the answer?

choices.misconception: I kept adding the digits of the answer until only one digit was left, and that always comes to 9 here.
I added the digits of the number itself, twenty 3s, instead of the digits of its square.
I saw the pattern of 1s, a 0, 8s and a final 9, wrote nineteen 1s and nineteen 8s, but forgot the final 9.
I treated 33 × 33 as the first case of my pattern, so I added 9 one time too many and got 18 + 19 × 9.

hints: Square 3, 33 and 333, and add up the digits each time.
Try small cases. The squares follow a clear digit pattern, and so do their digit sums. Check the rule on one more case before you trust it for twenty 3s.

solutions.reliable: Small cases: 3 × 3 = 9 (digit sum 9), 33 × 33 = 1089 (18), 333 × 333 = 110889 (27), 3333 × 3333 = 11108889 (36). With n threes the square is n - 1 ones, then a 0, then n - 1 eights, then a 9. For twenty 3s that is nineteen 1s, a 0, nineteen 8s and a 9, so the digit sum is 19 + 0 + 19 × 8 + 9 = 19 + 152 + 9 = 180. The transferable idea: a problem with a huge number is usually a pattern problem in disguise, and three or four small cases reveal it.
solutions.elegant: Each extra 3 adds one more 1 and one more 8 to the square, which adds 1 + 8 = 9 to the digit sum. A single 3 gives 9, so twenty 3s give 9 × 20 = 180.

whyOnTest: Nobody can multiply a 20-digit number by hand in a contest; trying 3, 33 and 333 first shows the pattern that makes the answer easy.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
